summary.short: Draft State Council regulation on minors' safe internet use. Applies to network services offered to minors in China, smart terminal makers and app distributors. Bars listed services to minors, requires a minors' mode for under-16 users, mandates user age identification, filing with regulators and administrative penalties. Effective date left blank in the draft.
summary.long: The draft State Council regulation would apply to network services provided to minors in China, to manufacturers of smart terminal products, and to app distribution platforms (Art. 2). It sets a principle of acting in minors' best interest and provides for minors' mode (Art. 3). It bars providers from offering listed services to minors, including stranger social networking, virtual intimate relationships, and live-streaming publishing for those under sixteen, with exceptions (Art. 4). Services listed in Art. 5, including social networking, games, and AI services that may affect minors' cognition, must be offered through a minors' mode to users under sixteen. Providers must identify minor users (Art. 6), manage harmful content (Art. 7), review recommendation algorithms and avoid models that induce emotional dependence or excessive spending (Art. 8), and offer appeal channels (Art. 9). Terminal makers and app distributors must support minors' mode and review applications (Art. 10). Minors' mode settings must be filed with provincial network authorities, with large platforms filing through them with the national authority (Art. 12). Penalties include warnings, confiscation, fines, suspension and closure (Arts. 18 to 20). Civil and criminal liability is preserved (Art. 21). The effective date is left blank.

notes: Draft for public comment; the published date is 2026-09-18 and the comment deadline is 2026-10-17. Art. 25 gives the effective date as '2026年 月 日起施行' with blanks, so no date is set. The three statutes in Art. 1 are coded as legal basis with null registry IDs. Art. 21 also cites them, plus the Regulations on the Online Protection of Minors and the Telecommunications Regulations, for handling other violations; the Regulations are coded as a cross-reference from Art. 12 para. 3. The explanatory note (说明) mentions the Provisions on the Online Protection of Children's Personal Information only as background; it is not coded. Penalty provisions (Arts. 18-20) are not coded here, as only relations, entities and notes were requested. Generic terms such as providers, schools and guardians are addressee classes and are not coded as entities.
